mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rate indicates tight monetary conditions, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX shows positive 20-day returns when FEDFUNDS is above 5% in over 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A significant rise in unemployment rate signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive when UNRATE rises as specified in over 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When employment growth (PAYEMS) is strong but unemployment (UNRATE) rises, it indicates potential labor market contradictions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Positive returns occur in over 50% of cases with these labor conditions.

mechanism_narrative: Rapid GDP growth during expansion signals strong economic activity, boosting S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Negative or flat returns occur in over 30% of cases with rapid GDP growth.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing industrial production (INDPRO) signals strong supply activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Returns are negative when INDPRO increases in over 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in real consumer spending (RSAFS) indicates weaker demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Positive returns occur in over 50% of cases with low RSAFS.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rate combined with slowing GDP growth signals economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Positive returns occur in over 30% of cases with these conditions.

mechanism_narrative: In a tight labor market (low UNRATE), a decline in employment (PAYEMS) signals potential weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Positive returns occur in over 40% of cases with these labor conditions.
